newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL SLIDES AFTER H1 EARNINGS. [CORRECTED 12:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MOL SLIDES AFTER H1 EARNINGS. [CORRECTED 12:10 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt fell in early trading on the Budapest Stock Exchange following the release of first half figures on Thursday, traders said.

"MOL's International Accounting Standard (IAS) net income was up 17 percent over the first half of last year, while its (share) price on the bourse is up 220 percent from a year ago," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"Income growth lags behind the (share) price growth, I see this behind the selling wave," he said.
At 1001 GMT MOL was at 4,320 forints, down 200 (Corrects from 300) from Wednesday's close.
Another trader said the results reinforced a downward trend, triggered by foreigners' across-the-board sales.

"The results contributed to the fall, but I think the main reason is that many investors decided to redirect their money to other markets within the region," said Laszlo Baranyai of Daewoo Securities.
MOL's fall of over eight percent in early trade, which slowed to around seven percent after half an hour of trade, contributed to a sharp drop in the BUX index.
At 1000 GMT the BUX index traded at 7,737.26 points, down 221.87 points or 2.79 percent. Many of the leading stocks, including OTP, Egis, TVK traded lower.

MOL's 14-day relative strength index (RSI) has fallen to a comfortable 49 percent on August 13 from 87.3 percent on August 6. A share is regarded overbought if its RSI value is above 70 percent and oversold if its RSI is below 30 percent.
